summary: Continuation of the verified prime-filtration baseline, now refining the R03.4 characteristic-zero-point argument into five declaration-sized nodes. The new proof separates nilpotent-uniformizer Artinianness, coefficient injection at a generic prime, an algebraically closed point with the exact kernel, finiteness of its field of values, and the integral local-map assembly. It does not assume flatness, a fixed residue field, or an unproved framed-lifting assertion. The complete local-field interpretation remains a required comparison with its existing owner, not a prerequisite of the algebraic theorem. Earlier baseline records and other-stage worklists are retained; the eight-stage blueprint remains partial. A further continuation adds four R03.3 nodes answering R03.6's requests: the catenary predicate with the Noetherian-local dimension-function criterion (Stacks 0ECF), Cohen–Macaulayness of regular local rings, and freeness of maximal-depth modules over a regular local base (Stacks 00NT, 00O7), with the domain property of regular local rings recorded as a gap.

nodes.title: Nilpotent uniformizer in a finite algebra
nodes.statement: Let O be a discrete valuation ring, pi an irreducible element of O, and A a commutative O-algebra finite as an O-module. If the image of pi is nilpotent in A, then A is Artinian. Neither localness or reducedness of A nor finiteness of the residue field of O is assumed.
hypotheses: All scalar actions come from the given unital O-algebra structure.
The zero algebra is allowed; a nilpotence witness of exponent zero forces this case.
proofSteps: Choose n with pi_A^n=0. The algebra map factors through O/(pi^n), since every multiple of pi^n maps to zero. The same finite O-generators generate A over that quotient: lift each quotient coefficient to O. Construct the quotient scalar action, not a new coefficient-ring type.

The uniformizer identity identifies (pi^n) with m_O^n. The pinned length formula gives O-module length n for this quotient; length_ne_top_iff and the finite-length equivalence make it Artinian as an O-module. Apply the pinned isArtinian_of_tower to the quotient scalar tower to make it an Artinian ring. Equivalently its ideals are O-submodules. This is scalar restriction, not finite cardinality.
Apply IsArtinianRing.of_finite to A over O/(pi^n). This includes n=0 by the zero-ring branch.
acceptance: For A=O/(pi^n)[t]/(t^2), the hypothesis holds and the conclusion is dimension at most zero, despite nonzero nilpotents.
For A=O[t]/(pi*t,t^2), pi is not nilpotent; the lemma must not infer Artinianness merely from pi-torsion.
The proof still applies when the residue field of O is infinite; it uses length, not the number of elements.

sources.match: This node supplies the general Artinian contradiction implicit in the point-existence argument; it is an explicit refinement, not a separately numbered KW lemma.
Reuses the full DVR quotient-length computation.
Supports the Artinian/finite-length step; pinned declarations above are the implementation baseline.

nodes.title: Coefficient injection at a generic prime
nodes.statement: For a DVR O, an irreducible pi, a commutative O-algebra A and a prime ideal q of A not containing pi_A, the coefficient map O -> A/q is injective. Finiteness and localness of A are unnecessary for this implication.
hypotheses: The image of pi is tested in q under the actual coefficient map.
The quotient uses the prime ideal q, so it is a nontrivial domain.
proofSteps: The kernel of O -> A/q is q contracted to O, which is a prime ideal.
A DVR has precisely one nonzero prime ideal, its maximal ideal (pi). If this contraction were nonzero, it would contain pi, contrary to the hypothesis. Hence the kernel is zero.
Translate zero kernel to injectivity of the ring homomorphism; retain the quotient coefficient map for the following scalar towers.
acceptance: For A=O and q=0 this is the original coefficient injection.
For A=O/(pi), its zero prime contains pi_A=0, so the hypothesis is rejected.
For O[t]/(t^2-pi*t), the two primes (t) and (t-pi) give two separate generic quotient maps, not a canonical chosen point.

sources.match: Makes explicit why the quotient in the source carries an injective coefficient-ring map.
The exact DVR prime classification, not a dimension theorem for an arbitrary local ring.

nodes.title: Algebraic point with prescribed generic kernel
nodes.statement: Let O be a commutative domain, A a module-finite commutative O-algebra, Omega an algebraically closed field with an injective O-algebra structure, and q a prime of A for which O -> A/q is injective. There is an O-algebra homomorphism f:A -> Omega with kernel exactly q.
hypotheses: Omega need not be a completion and need not be finite over Frac(O).
Use the chosen coefficient action on Omega and the quotient-induced action on A/q.
proofSteps: Put B=A/q. Its finite O-generating family is the image of one for A, hence B is integral and algebraic over O. Since B and Omega are domains and their O maps are injective, both O-module actions are torsion-free.

Apply the pinned IsAlgClosed.lift to B, not to A. Its inspected definition passes through Frac(B) and an embedding of Frac(B) into Omega over Frac(O). Both field maps and B -> Frac(B) are injective, so this particular lift is injective. Do not infer injectivity merely from the source being a domain.
Compose the lift with the quotient A -> B. Injectivity of the lift identifies the composite kernel with q; all coefficient identities follow from composition of the actual algebra maps.
acceptance: A=O[t]/(t^2) with q=(t) maps t to zero; the point need not be injective on A.
A product algebra can have several generic kernels. The statement constructs one point for the specified q, not an embedding of every finite algebra.
The coefficient injection into B is essential: a characteristic-p quotient cannot map as an O-algebra into a characteristic-zero Omega.

sources.locator: Corollary 4.7 proof, field of fractions of R/I
sources.match: This is the algebraically closed ambient-field form of the source quotient construction.
The source code constructs the needed embedding via fraction fields. No new algebraic-closure construction is planned.

nodes.title: Finite field generated by point values
nodes.statement: Let O be a commutative ring, K a field, and Omega a field in a compatible O -> K -> Omega scalar tower. For a module-finite commutative O-algebra A and an O-algebra homomorphism f:A -> Omega, the intermediate field E=K(f(A)) inside Omega is finite-dimensional over K. No injectivity or reducedness of A is assumed.
hypotheses: E is the existing IntermediateField.adjoin of the range of f, not a private field-of-values carrier.
Finiteness means module-finite A/O, not merely finitely generated A as an algebra.
proofSteps: Use Module.Finite.exists_fin' to choose a finite O-generating family a_i. Let W be the K-linear span in Omega of the f(a_i). Every f(a) lies in W by the O-linear expression for a and the coefficient compatibility of f.

The subspace W contains 1 and is closed under multiplication: expand a_i*a_j in the same O-generators, apply f, and then use K-bilinearity. Consequently W underlies a finite-dimensional K-subalgebra C of Omega.

C is integral over the field K by the finite/integral theorem. Algebra.IsIntegral.inv_mem shows it is closed under inverses in Omega, so the same subset defines an intermediate field. It contains f(A); conversely any intermediate field containing f(A) contains W. Thus this field is exactly E, which inherits the finite spanning family.
acceptance: For A=O the field of point values is K.
A finite nonreduced algebra such as O[t]/(t^2) gives E=K under t->0.
The hypothesis cannot be replaced by finite type: evaluation of O[t] at a transcendental element in a larger field generates an infinite-dimensional extension.

sources.locator: Corollary 4.7 proof, finiteness of the quotient fraction field
sources.match: Explicit finite-spanning proof of the field-finiteness step, with the chosen ambient-field convention.
Supplies the actual finite generating family.
Used after proving that the span is a finite subalgebra, not before.

nodes.title: Characteristic-zero integral points
nodes.statement: Let O be a DVR with fraction field K of characteristic zero; let Omega be a chosen algebraically closed extension of K, with the compatible O action. Let A be a commutative local O-algebra finite as an O-module, with 1 <= ringKrullDim(A). Then some finite intermediate field E/K in Omega admits an O-algebra map A -> integralClosure(O,E) that reflects units, and this integral closure is finite over O. No fixed target residue field or topology is asserted by this algebraic theorem. The complete-local-field interpretation and framed lifting remain distinct required extensions recorded below, not premises of this result.
hypotheses: The algebraic core only assumes a DVR, not completeness or a finite residue field. The ring-of-integers/topological interpretation uses the stated complete local-field supplier.
Do not replace positive dimension by A nonzero. Do not require A to be flat or torsion-free.
The integrated node ID is retained; its combined argument is refined into the four preceding nodes and this assembly.
proofSteps: Choose a uniformizer pi. If pi_A were nilpotent, nilpotent-uniformizer-artinian would make A Artinian. All its primes would be maximal, hence ringKrullDim(A)<=0 by the pinned dimension characterization, contradicting the premise.

Negate nilpotent_iff_mem_prime to select q prime avoiding pi_A. Apply generic-prime-coefficient-injection and algebraic-point-of-generic-prime to obtain f:A -> Omega with kernel q. The field E=K(f(A)) is finite by finite-field-of-point-values.

Corestrict f to E using its range inclusion and the induced O action. Each value is integral over O because A/O is finite, so corestrict once more to the existing integralClosure(O,E). In characteristic zero E/K is separable. IsIntegralClosure.finite applies since a DVR is Noetherian and integrally closed, showing that this closure is finite over O.

The map factors through an injective map B=A/q -> integralClosure(O,E). Every target element is integral over O and therefore over B by tower_top. RingHom.IsIntegral.isLocalHom makes that injective map reflect units. The quotient A -> B is local by IsLocalHom.of_surjective, and their composite is local by RingHom.isLocalHom_comp. The integral-injective lemma is NOT applied directly to A -> target, which generally has a kernel.
acceptance: A=O/(pi^n)[t]/(t^2) is finite and nonzero but has dimension zero, so is correctly rejected.
A=O[t]/(pi*t,t^2) has the point t->0 despite its nonzero pi-torsion. Flatness is not required.
A=O[t]/(t^2-pi*t) has the two points t->0 and t->pi, which can coincide on the special fiber. No uniqueness or special-fiber separation is asserted.

For O=Z_3 and A=O[t]/(t^2-18), any integral characteristic-zero point makes t/3 an integral unit whose square is 2. Its residue cannot lie in F_3. Thus a fixed-residue-field strengthening is not a general finite-algebra theorem. This is not an allegation that the source arithmetic corollary is false.
Without module-finiteness, A=k[t] viewed as an O-algebra has dimension one but pi acts by zero; the theorem must reject this example.

sources.match: Preserves the generic integral-point conclusion and refines its proof. The source-specific dimension, framed-category and residue-field bookkeeping remains separate.
Controls the finite integral closure without claiming locality over an incomplete DVR.
Supplies the quotient and composition steps after separately establishing the injective integral map.

remainingExtensions: Transport the algebraic point through LocalFieldsRamification Layer 0 integerRing_eq_integralClosure and the finite-extension topology, then prove continuity from maximal-ideal powers in the complete local-field regime. This is an unbuilt comparison requested below, not a prerequisite of the algebraic theorem.
Prove the retained framed-lifting target in the complete-local coefficient category, with its actual residue data, using a power-series presentation or compatible Artinian lifts.

nodes.title: Catenary rings
nodes.statement: A commutative ring R is catenary if for all prime ideals p ⊆ q (i) there is an integer bounding the lengths of all chains of primes p = p_0 ⊊ p_1 ⊊ ... ⊊ p_e = q, and (ii) any two saturated chains from p to q (chains in which each step p_i ⊊ p_{i+1} is a covering relation, no prime strictly between) have the same length. Chains are LTSeries in the poset PrimeSpectrum R; a saturated chain has every step a covering relation ⋖.
hypotheses: No Noetherian or local hypothesis in the definition.
The boundedness clause is part of the definition (Stacks 00NI); for a Noetherian ring it is automatic, since chains from p to q have length at most ht q < ∞.
proofSteps: Definition: Ring.IsCatenary R := for all p ≤ q in PrimeSpectrum R, (∃ n, every LTSeries from p to q has length ≤ n) ∧ (any two LTSeries from p to q whose steps are all covering relations have equal length).
acceptance: Saturation matters: k[x, y] is catenary although 0 ⊂ (x, y) and 0 ⊂ (x) ⊂ (x, y) have different lengths; only the second is saturated.
The equal-length clause is not automatic for Noetherian local domains: Nagata's ring A[x]_{m'} (Stacks 02JE) has dimension 3 and a maximal chain (0) ⊂ pA[x]_{m'} ⊂ m' of length 2.
Boundedness is part of the definition: for Noetherian rings it holds by finiteness of heights, so the clause only restricts non-Noetherian rings.

uses.how: Taylor's Lemma 2.2(2) assumes A catenary; R03.6 states it in the dimension-function form, which catenary-iff-dimension-function identifies with this predicate for Noetherian local rings.
'explicit catenarity and excellence hypotheses rather than geometric conclusions for arbitrary local rings'.

nodes.title: Catenarity of a Noetherian local ring as a dimension function
nodes.statement: Let (A, m) be a Noetherian local ring. Then A is catenary if and only if dim A/p = dim A/q + 1 for all primes p ⋖ q of A (q covers p: p ⊊ q with no prime strictly between). Here dim is ringKrullDim of the quotient ring.
hypotheses: A Noetherian and local, so dim A is finite.
The right-hand side is exactly the hypothesis hcat of R03.6's NearlyFaithful.of_quotient_of_isSMulRegular.
proofSteps: For a prime p, dim A/p is the Krull dimension of the poset V(p) of primes containing p (Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient), and it is finite because dim A/p ≤ dim A < ∞ (Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient_le and ringKrullDim_lt_top, the FiniteRingKrullDim instance for Noetherian local rings in KrullsHeightTheorem). So every chain of primes starting at p has length at most dim A/p (Mathlib Order.LTSeries.length_le_krullDim), and some chain of length dim A/p starts at p; since m contains every prime, it may be taken to end at m.

A chain of maximal length between two primes is saturated: otherwise inserting a prime strictly between two consecutive terms (Mathlib RelSeries.insertNth) gives a longer chain. Hence there is a saturated chain from p to m of length dim A/p.

(⇒) Let p ⋖ q. By the second step there is a saturated chain from q to m of length dim A/q; putting p in front gives a saturated chain from p to m of length dim A/q + 1. There is also a saturated chain from p to m of length dim A/p. By the equal-length clause of catenary, dim A/p = dim A/q + 1.

(⇐) Boundedness: by the first step, any chain from p to q has length at most dim A/p < ∞. Equal lengths: along a saturated chain p = p_0 ⋖ p_1 ⋖ ... ⋖ p_e = q the hypothesis gives dim A/p_i = dim A/p_{i+1} + 1, so e = dim A/p − dim A/q, which does not depend on the chain.
acceptance: Locality is needed: let A be k[x, y] localized at the complement of (x, y) ∪ (x − 1). By prime avoidance its primes are those of k[x, y] inside (x, y) or inside (x − 1), so A is a catenary Noetherian domain (a localization of k[x, y], Stacks 00NJ) with maximal ideals (x, y)A of height 2 and (x − 1)A of height 1. Then (0) ⋖ (x − 1)A, but dim A/(0) = 2 while dim A/(x − 1)A = 0.

Catenary does not give equidimensional: A = k⟦x, y, z⟧/(xz, yz) (a plane and a line through the closed point) satisfies the dimension-function condition, e.g. (x, y) ⋖ m with 1 = 0 + 1 and (z) ⋖ (x, z) with 2 = 1 + 1, yet its minimal primes have dimensions 2 and 1. R03.6's lifting lemma therefore keeps its separate equidimensionality hypothesis.
On Nagata's ring A[x]_{m'} (Stacks 02JE) the condition fails along (0) ⋖ pA[x]_{m'} ⋖ m': dim of the ring is 3, so dim A/(0) = 3, while dim along the saturated chain is 2.

uses.how: R03.6 requested this equivalence (its request to R03.3, Stacks 0ECF) so that Taylor's catenarity hypothesis can be stated as a predicate; its Lean hypothesis hcat is the right-hand side.

sources.excerpt: Let (A, m) be a Noetherian local ring. The following are equivalent: (1) A is catenary, and (2) p ↦ dim(A/p) is a dimension function on Spec(A).
sources.match: Exactly this equivalence; for p ↦ dim A/p the strict-decrease clause of a dimension function is automatic, so (2) is the covering condition stated here. Stacks proves it through Topology Lemmas 5.20.2 and 5.20.4; the proof here is the direct chain argument.

nodes.title: A regular local ring has a regular sequence of length its dimension
nodes.statement: Let A be a regular local ring of dimension d. Then every minimal set of generators x_1, ..., x_d of the maximal ideal is an A-regular sequence; in particular A has an A-regular sequence in m of length d = ringKrullDim A, so A is Cohen–Macaulay (depth A = dim A).
hypotheses: A regular local: Noetherian local with m generated by dim A elements (Mathlib IsRegularLocalRing).
proofSteps: Induction on d. For d = 0 the empty sequence works.
For d > 0, A is a domain (gap: Stacks 00NP, via the associated graded ring of 00NO), so x_1 ≠ 0 is a nonzerodivisor; x_1 ∈ m.

Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient_span_singleton_succ_eq_ringKrullDim_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors gives dim A/(x_1) = d − 1, and the images of x_2, ..., x_d generate the maximal ideal of A/(x_1). So A/(x_1) is regular local of dimension d − 1 (Mathlib isRegularLocalRing_iff: a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal is generated by dim elements), and by induction x_2, ..., x_d is A/(x_1)-regular. Hence x_1, ..., x_d is A-regular (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular unfolds as x_1 regular followed by a regular sequence on the quotient).
acceptance: Regularity is needed: A = k⟦x, y⟧/(x², xy) is Noetherian local of dimension 1, but the nonzero element x is killed by the whole maximal ideal (x, y), so every element of m is a zero divisor and A has no regular sequence of length 1.
The converse fails: k⟦x, y⟧/(xy) has dimension 1 and the regular element x + y, so it is Cohen–Macaulay, but its maximal ideal needs two generators, so it is not regular.
Dimension one: for a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ, the sequence (ϖ) is regular of length 1.

uses.how: depth A = dim A enters the Auslander–Buchsbaum computation pd M = depth A − depth M = 0.

sources.excerpt: Let R be a regular local ring and let x_1, ..., x_d be a minimal set of generators for the maximal ideal m. Then x_1, ..., x_d is a regular sequence, and each R/(x_1, ..., x_c) is a regular local ring of dimension d − c. In particular R is Cohen-Macaulay.
sources.match: The statement; the domain property it uses is Lemma 10.106.2 (00NP), recorded as a gap.

nodes.title: Maximal-depth modules over a regular local ring are free
nodes.statement: Let A be a regular local ring and M a finite A-module that has an M-regular sequence r_1, ..., r_n in the maximal ideal of length n = dim A (that is, M ≠ 0 and depth M ≥ dim A: M is maximal Cohen–Macaulay). Then M is free.
hypotheses: M finite over A; the regular sequence lies in m and has length ringKrullDim A. RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular includes M/(r)M ≠ 0, so M ≠ 0.
Stated with a regular sequence because the pinned Mathlib has no module depth; this is the form R03.6 uses.
proofSteps: depth M ≥ dim A from the given sequence, and depth M ≤ dim Supp M ≤ dim A by the integrated R03.3 node; so depth M = dim A = d, and M ≠ 0 (Mathlib RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular.nontrivial).
A regular local ring has finite global dimension (the integrated R03.3 node), so pd_A M < ∞.
depth A = d by regular-local-cohen-macaulay.
Auslander–Buchsbaum (the integrated R03.3 node) gives pd_A M + depth M = depth A, so pd_A M = 0: M is projective.
A finite projective module is flat (Mathlib instance Module.Flat.of_projective), and a finite flat module over a local ring is free (Mathlib Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing).
acceptance: Regularity of A is needed: over the dual numbers k[ε] (dimension 0) the empty sequence has length 0 = dim, but k = k[ε]/(ε) is not free.
Maximal depth is needed: over k⟦x⟧ (regular, dimension 1), k = k⟦x⟧/(x) has depth 0 and is not free.

Compatibility with ModularCurves 4D (required by RS-08): for a finite local homomorphism A → B of regular local rings of the same dimension d, a regular system of parameters of B is a B-regular sequence of length d (regular-local-cohen-macaulay); together with a system of parameters of A it shows depth_A B = d, so B is free over A. This recovers 4D's miracle flatness for finite maps of regular local rings of equal dimension rather than restating it.

sources.match: The statement; the proof here uses Auslander–Buchsbaum and finite global dimension from the integrated R03.3 node instead of Stacks' induction through 00N6 and 00NS.

The consumer must still prove the zero case, transport its prime-quotient case through linear equivalences by naturality, and prove its nonsplit extension step. No generic prime-filtration request to R03.3 is necessary.

Reuse the Layer 0 intermediate-field adapters. This comparison extends the algebraic theorem; it is not needed to construct its map to integralClosure.

For the separate framed-lifting target retained from the integrated R03.4 node, provide the exact complete-local coefficient-category lifting interface: a proved power-series presentation with compatible residue data, or a formally smooth continuous map together with compatible Artinian quotient lifts and an inverse-limit realization. gaps.title: Regular local rings are domains
gaps.detail: Stacks Lemma 10.106.2 (00NP): any regular local ring is a domain, proved from Lemma 10.106.1 (00NO), gr_m(R) ≅ κ[X_1, ..., X_d]. Neither is in the pinned Mathlib (no IsDomain instance for IsRegularLocalRing) and no layer of the atlas plans the associated-graded computation; it is generic local algebra owned by R03.3 under RS-08 and must be decomposed there (Hilbert–Samuel function of R and of the polynomial ring).
